stories.title: Economic and technical optimal sizing and placement of the hybrid energy resources in the electrical grid considering uncertainties
stories.description: The integration of hybrid energy resources in the electrical grids is essential for improving sustainability and reducing dependence on conventional fossil-fuel generation. Hence, installation of these energy resources is required to maximize their technical and economic benefits while maintaining secure and stable grid operation. This paper focuses on a multi-objective optimization framework to identify the best installation and sizing of hybrid energy resources, considering the stochastic characteristics associated with renewable generation, such as photovoltaic (PV) and wind turbine (WT) systems. The stochastic aspects of renewable generation are represented using the point estimate method, enabling the framework to account for variations in renewable resource availability. The multi-objective functions for the optimal installation and sizing of hybrid energy resources are developed with a focus on operational costs, Voltage Stability Index (VSI), and power losses. Two case studies are provided to validate the proposed algorithm, examining different configurations of hybrid energy resources in IEEE 33-bus and IEEE 118-bus test systems. The optimal sizing of hybrid energy resources in the IEEE 33-bus test system result in a 3.68% reduction in operating costs, a 42.89% decrease in power losses, and a 0.19% improvement in the VSI. Also, minimization rate of the operational costs and power losses, and improvement of VSI for IEEE 118-bus test system are equal to 9.3%, 13.23% and 0.3%, respectively.
